current_date: 2024 (document titled 'Tyneside Validation Checklist 2024'; no day or month of adoption in the text)
current_evidence: Gateshead's 'Apply for planning permission and validation requirements' page (article/5362) still links this exact PDF as 'Tyneside Validation Checklist 2024' and mentions no newer version or consultation. Newcastle's shared validation page hosts the same 2024 checklist (file 'Tyneside Validation Checklist Jan 25 - Final with bookmarks'), which states 'This latest document supersedes the validation checklist published in 2019'.

issues.detail: Grokbot also read the superseded 2019 'Tyne and Wear validation list' (media/6692) and mixed its content into the workbook alongside the 2024 list. Rows sourced from the 2019 document include: Householder 'Minerals / Waste specific statements', Full 'Block plan / Site plan', 'Cycle parking details', the second 'Ecological Survey', 'Heritage Statement' and 'Travel Plan'. Tab_items from 2019 include the location/site plan standards, the housing space statement, 'Failure to submit...' and about 8 signature-redaction snippets. All of these should be removed or re-sourced to the 2024 list.
issues.evidence: 2024 checklist: 'This latest document supersedes the validation checklist published in 2019.' docs_read includes .../media/6692/Tyne-and-Wear-validation-list-2019/...

issues.detail: The List date 2024-09-01 comes from PDF metadata (and the URL timestamp). The document text gives only '2024'. 'Outdated (>2y)? = Yes' is misleading, because the council's page still presents this as the current Tyneside checklist. The 'Planning page' field is a print view of article/27094, which no longer shows the checklist; the live page that links it is article/5362.
issues.evidence: Article/5362 links 'Tyneside Validation Checklist (PDF, 1 MB)' with no adoption date. Article/27094 fetch showed only general 'The application must be accompanied by:' text.

issues.detail: Several rows are placed under application types that the source expressly excludes. (1) Householder 'Coal Mining / Land Stability Risk Assessment': the trigger itself says householder extensions are an exception. (2) Householder 'Minerals / Waste specific statements': this carries the same 2019 coal-mining text, including the householder exception, under the wrong name. (3) Under 'Change of use - prior approval': 'Block plan / Site plan', 'Design Code / Masterplan' and 'Landscaping scheme' are all triggered by text that excludes change of use ('excluding applications for change of use only'; 'other than wholly change of use/conversion applications'), and 'Structural Survey' applies to planning applications to convert rural buildings, not GPDO prior approvals. (4) Reserved matters shows '(none)', although the Sustainability Statement trigger names 'major reserved matter applications'. (5) Demolition in cons area shows '(none)', although a Heritage Statement is required for demolition in conservation areas (Checklist 3). (6) Listed building consent omits the DAS (Note 7). The remaining approximately 45 rows are all marked 'INFERRED ... placed under Full planning', even where the source names thresholds or types (for example Note 12 Affordable Housing, Note 20 Housing Space Standards).
issues.evidence: Note 15: 'with the exception of householder extensions or alterations, changes of use and shop front alterations'; Note 22: 'other than wholly change of use/conversion applications'; Note 19: 'Other applications in conservation areas, including demolition'.

issues.detail: Several requirement labels carry another item's text. 'Schedule of works (listed building)' and 'Construction (Environmental) Management Plan' both carry the SuDS Construction Method Statement text. 'Noise Impact Assessment' carries ventilation/extraction text, while 'Odour / Dust / Vibration assessment' carries the Acoustic and Vibration trigger (the two are swapped). 'Lighting Assessment' carries the daylight/sunlight proximity-to-windows trigger. 'Advertisement drawings / illumination' carries floodlighting text plus data-protection boilerplate. 'Planning Obligations / S106 Heads of Terms' carries BNG-obligation text. 'Planning Statement' carries the affordable housing statement questions. 'Sequential / Exception Test (flood)' carries document-title wording instead of its trigger (new development in Flood Zones 2 and 3, with householder, under-250 sqm non-residential extensions and renewables exempt).
issues.evidence: Trigger excerpts in app_type_rows; Note 17: Sequential Test 'Required for new development in Flood Zones 2 and 3'.

issues.detail: Many triggers are cut-off fragments without the actual threshold. 'Design and Access Statement' = 'Design and Access Statement (if required) 8.'; 'Drainage Strategy / SuDS' = '...within the NE LLFA area.' (actual: major development); 'Arboricultural Impact Assessment' = '(see section 35)'; 'Archaeological Assessment' = 'When is this required? Archaeological desk based assessment' (actual: near Scheduled Monuments, the Hadrian's Wall corridor, Roman fort vicus areas, greenfield 1ha+); 'Tall buildings / Wind' = 'near other tall buildings.'; 'Minerals' = 'sterilisation of mineral resources.' (actual: non-mineral development over 1ha); 'Marketing' = 'conservation areas Marketing information will not always be required.' (actual: loss of retail in primary frontages, non-allocated uses on employment land, demolition of listed, locally listed or conservation-area buildings). Gateshead-specific thresholds are also missing: Affordable Housing Statement 10+ units; Housing Space Standards for all new homes, with M4(2) at 25% for 15+ dwellings; and land contamination screening for single dwellings on undeveloped land in Gateshead.
issues.evidence: Notes 12, 14, 15, 20, 21, 24 of the Tyneside Validation Checklist 2024.

issues.detail: Requirements not captured: Overheating Assessment and Mitigation Requirements (Note 26), which is absent everywhere. Simple FRA for householder extensions in Flood Zones 2 and 3 (Note 17), absent from Householder. FRA in Flood Zones 2 and 3 for changes of use. Habitats Regulations Assessment proximity trigger (e.g. within 500m of the coast; Note 16). Landscape Strategy/Masterplan (Note 22) and Landscaping Details (Note 23) as they actually apply, to major and full applications, rather than to change of use. Heritage Statement for major applications in or affecting conservation areas and for non-designated assets (Note 19). Ecological Impact Assessment for non-householder schemes affecting semi-natural habitat (Note 16).
issues.evidence: Note 17: 'A simple FRA is needed for householder extensions in Flood Zones 2 and 3'; contents list 'Note 26 Overheating Assessment and Mitigation Requirements'.

issues.detail: Several items are listed as requirements but are not. 'Employment / Economic Statement': the source says it 'would not be required for validation purposes'. 'Pre-application advice / engagement details': its trigger is table-of-contents text. Most of the 29 tab_items are boilerplate or references: the data-protection/signature-redaction sentence (about 9 times, some with page numbers or 'Checklist 2:' run on), 'LINKS TO SUPPORTING GUIDANCE DOCUMENTS ... MAY BE SUBJECT TO CHANGE', 'The submission of paper copies ... is not recommended', 'Failure to submit the required information will result in your application being made invalid', 'Advice from the Environment Agency ... 445.pdf', lists of Core Strategy policies and viability guidance links, and SPA/Ramsar definitional fragments.
issues.evidence: Trigger: 'Applicants can also submit an Economic Statement ... but this would not be required for validation purposes.'

issues.detail: The data-protection sentence is repeated across about 9 tab_items. Location plan, site plan and housing space items appear twice (2019 and 2024 versions). 'Ecological Survey' appears twice under Full (2019 and 2024). 'Floor plans / Elevations' and 'Existing and proposed site levels' share one trigger, as do 'Construction Management Plan' and 'Schedule of works'.
issues.evidence: tab_items 'Submission rules' section; app_type_rows Full planning.

summary: Grokbot's link is still the current Gateshead/Tyneside 2024 checklist, although the PDF refused automated fetching; contents were checked against the identical copy on Newcastle's site. The extraction blends in the superseded 2019 list, mislabels or swaps many triggers, misses the overheating assessment and the householder FRA rule, and places coal mining under Householder and landscaping under change of use, although the source excludes both.
grok_review: Reviewed by Grok 5 Nov 2026; Claude responded to every disagreement the same day.
